decisions.reason: The citrus harvesting crate had only limited website visibility, serves a relatively narrow agricultural niche, and is easier to abandon when results disappoint because the firm's public and strategic commitment to it was modest.

The foldable large container received the strongest public backing with its own page across two years and sits squarely in the firm's core reusable logistics strategy, making management likely to persist and attribute weak uptake to temporary market conditions.

The stackable plastic crate fits the portfolio but never received strong standalone promotion, so with weak visible traction management would likely reallocate effort to better-established crate lines or new developments.

A medium-duty rackable pallet is close to the firm's core pallet business and can be justified as a strategically relevant extension, so escalation of commitment would favor giving it more time despite limited early visibility.

Although initially launched prominently, the spill-retention pallet was quickly reduced to a mention and is less central than mainstream returnable transport packaging, making continued commitment harder to defend.

The plastic pallet with load retainers had an initially visible launch and remains tightly aligned with the firm's pallet offering and customer value proposition, so management would be inclined to continue rather than admit failure.
